title: Reflected XSS context confirmation
summary: Identify where reflected input lands in the HTML, attribute, URL, or script context and use context-appropriate harmless markers to confirm executable behavior.
preconditions: The tester can receive or observe the crafted response in an authorized browser.
The input is reflected in a response processed by a browser.
verification_method: Inspect the raw response and identify the exact parsing context around the reflection.
Load the unique marker payload in a controlled browser and confirm JavaScript execution.
Test an encoded control to distinguish execution from literal reflection.
known_failures: Framework output encoding may block one metacharacter but not another context.
CSP can prevent execution even when unsafe reflection exists.
DOM sanitizers can rewrite the payload after the raw response is captured.
steps: Inject a unique alphanumeric marker and locate every reflection in raw and rendered output.
Classify the context as HTML text, attribute, URL, script, or DOM sink.
Use a benign execution marker matching that context rather than a generic payload.
Confirm the marker executes from the target origin and capture browser evidence.
Check whether storage, caching, or a server-side transformation changes the final content.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting; CWE-79
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Stored XSS persistence and sink analysis
summary: Trace whether submitted content persists and is later rendered unencoded for another user or privileged view.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to create and remove test content.
A second read path, role, or preview page can be observed safely.
verification_method: Submit a unique marker and retrieve it through the intended second read path.
Compare the stored raw value with the DOM and execute a harmless browser marker.
Delete or clean up the test record after evidence is captured.
known_failures: Input filtering may permit storage but encode the value at output.
An admin-only sink may be unreachable with the current test role.
Background sanitizers or moderation can alter stored content asynchronously.
steps: Choose a low-impact field such as a profile note or draft comment.
Submit a unique marker without executable syntax and locate its stored form.
Reopen the record through every relevant rendering path.
Introduce a harmless context-appropriate executable marker and capture browser evidence.
Verify cleanup and note which role, endpoint, and field are affected.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Stored Cross Site Scripting; CWE-79
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: SSRF to an internal service
summary: Determine whether a server-side fetch primitive can be redirected from an allowed external resource to an internal address or service.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to request internal lab endpoints.
The target feature performs a server-side URL fetch.
verification_method: Compare an allowed external URL with a loopback URL and record status, body, timing, and redirects.
Use a dedicated callback or local lab service to prove the request originates server-side.
Test DNS rebinding or redirect controls only when explicitly in scope and safely isolated.
known_failures: An allowlist can permit a hostname but revalidate the resolved IP.
The fetch client may block loopback while allowing private network ranges.
Errors can distinguish reachable services without returning their response body.
steps: Identify a feature that fetches images, feeds, webhooks, documents, or previews.
Confirm a normal external URL works and capture the server-side behavior.
Replace it with a loopback URL and then a controlled private lab service.
Inspect response time, status, body, and DNS or proxy telemetry.
Map the reachable service and document impact without scanning unrelated networks.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Server-Side Request Forgery; CWE-918
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: SSRF access to cloud instance metadata
summary: Test whether a server-side fetch reaches the cloud metadata address and whether authentication or hop controls prevent credential exposure.
preconditions: Testing is explicitly authorized against an isolated cloud lab account.
The target performs a server-side HTTP request.
verification_method: Use a non-secret metadata root path and compare response behavior with a blocked address.
Verify provider-specific response structure without printing credentials.
Confirm whether IMDSv2-style headers or metadata proxy controls are enforced.
known_failures: Cloud providers and proxy layers use different metadata addresses and authentication requirements.
A blacklist may block the literal IP while allowing alternate representations.
SSRF may be blind, requiring timing or callback evidence instead of response contents.
steps: Confirm the application can fetch a controlled external callback.
Request a harmless metadata root or region identifier through the vulnerable URL parameter.
Record only the minimum non-sensitive response fields needed to prove access.
Test provider-documented alternate hostnames or redirect paths only within the lab scope.
Report credential exposure risk and rotation requirements if secret material was reachable.

provenance.source_ref: MITRE CWE-918; NIST SP 800-145 cloud computing definition
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Path traversal through file selection parameters
summary: Test whether a filename or path parameter can escape the intended directory and access a known file outside that root.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to read only harmless lab files.
The application exposes file download, preview, template, or export behavior.
verification_method: Compare a valid in-scope file with traversal and normalized control paths.
Use a harmless known file and verify content origin rather than only status code.
Confirm that canonicalization or a base-directory control removes the behavior.
known_failures: The server may normalize the path before concatenation, preventing traversal.
A whitelist can resolve the same filename differently on Windows and POSIX.
Downloads may succeed for missing paths using a generic error page.
steps: Identify a parameter that selects a file or template name.
Capture a valid response and the exact in-scope file root.
Request a harmless parent-directory file with platform-appropriate separators.
Compare content hashes or known markers to prove the file changed.
Test encoding and normalization variants only after the basic traversal signal is understood.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Path Traversal; CWE-22
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Unrestricted file upload execution assessment
summary: Determine whether uploaded files can be stored with dangerous names, types, or locations that lead to server-side execution or content trust bypass.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to upload controlled files to an isolated target.
Uploaded content can be retrieved or executed through a known path.
verification_method: Upload a harmless unique marker file and verify storage, returned path, content type, and retrieval.
Test extension and content-type mismatches separately and record server responses.
Confirm execution only with an authorized minimal test file and clean it up.
known_failures: The server may rename files or store them outside the web root.
MIME sniffing can change browser behavior without server execution.
A CDN or object store may sanitize extensions after upload.
steps: Identify accepted file fields, size limits, and the retrieval URL.
Upload a benign file with a unique content marker and locate the stored object.
Compare allowed extension, declared MIME type, and server-detected content type.
Test one extension boundary at a time and check whether the file is served or executed.
Remove test artifacts and report the exact storage and execution conditions.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Unrestricted File Upload; CWE-434
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Open redirect through return URL parameters
summary: Test whether a redirect parameter accepts an external destination without a strict allowlist or signed state.
preconditions: The tester controls a harmless external landing page or callback URL.
The application returns a Location header or client-side navigation based on input.
verification_method: Submit a controlled external URL and inspect Location or browser navigation.
Compare with a relative path and an allowed same-origin path.
Check whether redirect validation rejects only the literal scheme or host form.
known_failures: The server may allowlist a hostname suffix but still reject the controlled domain.
Client-side routers can navigate without a server Location header.
Redirects may be disabled after login or by a feature flag.
steps: Find a parameter named for continuation, return, next, redirect, or callback behavior.
Capture a baseline redirect to a valid same-origin page.
Submit a harmless controlled external URL and inspect status, Location, and browser flow.
Test relative and malformed URL controls to map the validator.
Report whether redirect chaining creates phishing, token leakage, or SSRF impact.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Open Redirections; CWE-601
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: CORS origin reflection with credentials
summary: Determine whether arbitrary Origin values are reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with credential support.
preconditions: The tester can send a controlled Origin header.
A sensitive authenticated endpoint or session cookie is available in the lab.
verification_method: Compare allowed and disallowed Origin values and inspect ACAO and ACAC headers.
Check preflight behavior and whether credentialed responses are readable cross-origin.
Confirm behavior through a browser rather than relying only on header reflection.
known_failures: Reflecting Origin without credentials may be low impact or intentional for public data.
The response may be cached with the first Origin and produce inconsistent results.
A wildcard cannot be used with credentials, so an application may choose a mirrored origin instead.
steps: Send a normal same-origin request and a request with a controlled external Origin.
Record Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, Vary, and status.
Send an OPTIONS preflight with methods and headers relevant to the sensitive endpoint.
Use a browser page from the controlled origin to test whether the response is readable.
Prove impact with non-destructive data only and document the exact credential and endpoint scope.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing Cross Origin Resource Sharing; CWE-942
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.
